thought.text: The container user (uid 1000) can't write to the root-owned workspace. In a real devcontainer the workspace is owned by the container user. Let me fix ownership and re-run setup:

reasoning_content:
Confirmed: /workspace is owned by root (0:0), and the container user (uid 1000, vscode) cannot write. This is a mismatch between the environment (workspace mounted as root-owned) and the devcontainer's expectation (workspace owned by vscode uid 1000).

I'll chown the workspace to 1000:1000 so that the container user can write. This is the standard approach. Since this is the shared installation workspace and the devcontainer assumes ownership, chowning is the correct response.

action.command: chown -R 1000:1000 /workspace 2>&1; echo "CHOWN_EXIT=$?"; docker exec zammad-devcontainer-devcontainer-1 bash -lc 'stat -c "%u:%g" /workspaces/workspace; touch /workspaces/workspace/.writetest && echo "WRITE_OK" && rm -f /workspaces/workspace/.writetest'

tool_call.name: terminal
tool_call.arguments: {"command": "chown -R 1000:1000 /workspace 2>&1; echo \"CHOWN_EXIT=$?\"; docker exec zammad-devcontainer-devcontainer-1 bash -lc 'stat -c \"%u:%g\" /workspaces/workspace; touch /workspaces/workspace/.writetest && echo \"WRITE_OK\" && rm -f /workspaces/workspace/.writetest'", "security_risk": "HIGH", "summary": "Chown workspace to container user"}
